title: Queens Public Library network disrupted by ransomware attack, services partly restored two weeks on
date_note: NY1 says the library first reported a systemwide outage on Wednesday 4 November; QNS dates identification of the attack to 4 November.
place: Queens, New York, United States (library system serving the borough)
geo_basis: borough served by the library system; headquarters address not read
summary: NY1 and QNS report a ransomware attack on the Queens Public Library, which first reported a systemwide network outage on 4 November. As of QNS's 18 November article the website, app and renewals were still unavailable and public computers worked at seven of 66 branches. The NYPD said it was working with the FBI on a cybersecurity incident. QNS says the ransom amount and the attackers are not known.
plain: Queens Public Library's computer systems were knocked offline in early November. Reporters call it ransomware. Some services are back, but the website, app and renewals were still down on 18 November.
exec: A US public library system's website and most public computers were still down two weeks after a reported ransomware attack; no timeline for full restoration has been given.
impact: QNS (18 Nov): website, mobile app and renewals unavailable; public computers back at seven of 66 branches; checkout and return machines restored; all branches open.

validation.note: NY1 (5 Nov) and QNS (18 Nov) are independent publishers that each describe a ransomware attack on the library; NY1 quotes the NYPD calling it a cybersecurity incident. Neither article quotes the library itself using the word ransomware, so status stays developing. Neither says whether patron data was accessed.

review.note: Compared title, date (4 Nov outage), 7 of 66 branches, website/app/renewals status, NYPD/FBI statement, unknown ransom/attackers, status developing against NY1 (5 Nov) and QNS (18 Nov)
